column1: What does multiplying by \( i \) do geometrically?
column2: Turns the point 90° counterclockwise around 0. Length stays the same.

column1: Modulus and conjugate of \( a + bi \)?

column2: Multiply the lengths, add the angles.
\( e^{2\pi i k/n} \) for \( k = 0..n-1 \): a regular \( n \)-gon on the unit circle. They sum to 0.

column1: What does \( z^2 \) do to a point \( re^{i\theta} \)?
column2: Squares the length and doubles the angle: \( r^2 e^{2i\theta} \).

column1: What does an analytic function do locally?
column2: Rotates and scales tiny shapes by the complex number \( f'(z_0) \).
A map that preserves angles. Analytic maps are conformal where \( f' \neq 0 \).
The integral of an analytic function around a closed loop is 0.
\( \oint f\,dz = 2\pi i \sum \) residues inside the loop.
Every nontrivial zero of \( \zeta(s) \) has real part 1/2.
